newsitem.title: BERMUDA: Sphere Drake pleased with profit turnaround.
newsitem.headline: Sphere Drake pleased with profit turnaround.

text.p: Sphere Drake Holdings Limited has announced strong results for the fourth quarter and the year ended December 31, 1996.

For the full year of 1996, the company saw a rise in operating income from continuing operations, excluding realised investment gains/losses net of tax, to $36.0 million, compared with an operating loss of $19.8 million for 1995.
Net income for 1996 was $26.5 million compared with the previous year, representing a turnaround of $44.4 million despite restructuring costs in the fourth quarter of $8.6 million before tax.
Further costs of up to $7 million before tax are expected in future periods, the company said.

For the fourth quarter of 1996, operating income from continuing operations was $8.6 million, compared with an operating loss of $52.2 million for the corresponding period in 1995. The net loss for the fourth quarter of 1996 was $0.4 million compared with a loss of $49.9 million the previous year.

The company said losses from discontinued operations of $10.8 million for the quarter and $14.2 million for the year encompass all marine insurance lines from which Sphere Drake withdrew as part of recent strategic restructuring aimed at concentrating resources on those lines of business where it can offer meaningful capacity and support to its customers, lead business and/or influence the terms of trade and add value through demonstrated underwriting expertise.

Michael Watson, president and chief executive Officer of Sphere Drake Holdings Limited, said: "I am very pleased with our 1996 results. We have delivered earnings in line with our expectations despite tough market conditions, and we have delivered an attractive return to shareholders after providing appropriately for restructuring costs in the fourth quarter."
"Our return to profitability last year undoubtedly owes much to the further excellent results from our property catastrophe business," he added. --Reuters Insurance News +44 171 542 2770
